key_insight: AlB₁₂–Al detonation coatings improved the wear resistance of steel 45, with AB70 showing stable tribological performance under the tested friction conditions.
engineering_relevance: These coatings offer a potential wear-protection option for steel components exposed to sliding friction.
method: Deposited AB70 (70 wt.% AlB₁₂, 30 wt.% Al) and AB30 (30 wt.% AlB₁₂, 70 wt.% Al) using a DNEPR-5M detonation-spray system.
Characterized coating thickness, hardness, and tribological behavior under varying sliding speeds and loads.
Examined post-friction surfaces and identified oxidative and adhesive-abrasive wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports coating thicknesses of approximately 170–200 μm and AB70 friction coefficients of 0.21–0.38 with wear rates of 3.3–8.6 μm/km; coated samples outperformed uncoated steel 45 in wear resistance.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify test-load and sliding-speed ranges, repeatability, or adhesion strength, limiting assessment of service suitability.
paper_title: Structure and properties of AlB12-Al detonation coatings on steel 45
